key_insight: OCFormer learns a physics-informed map from independent latent dynamics to collision-constrained multi-agent trajectories, enabling near-optimal planning for unseen start and goal configurations.
engineering_relevance: Amortized inference could accelerate coordinated robot or drone navigation without solving a new optimal control problem from scratch for every configuration.
method: Use a transformer to map analytically tractable latent dynamics into the interacting physical system.
Train with Pontryagin Hamiltonian ODE residuals and boundary matching, without precomputed trajectories.
Preserve agent permutation equivariance through self-attention and adapt to distribution shifts with L-BFGS fine-tuning.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 2D and 3D navigation experiments with up to 128 agents, approximately 220 ms single-pass inference, and adaptation to out-of-distribution perturbations in seconds.
watch_item: Physics-informed loss minimization alone does not establish guaranteed collision avoidance or optimality for unseen configurations.
paper_title: A Transformer-based Approach for Real-time Multi-agent Path Planning with Varying Initial/Final Conditions
